title: runtime: /actions answers a driver string code (SQLITE_BUSY) as 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with declaredCode, where /data answers the same throw 500 DATABASE_ERROR
body:
domain:server#6 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ

## What is wrong

The same thrown driver error gets two different answers depending on the door.

- `/data` answers a driver error carrying a string code such as `SQLITE_BUSY` as **500 `DATABASE_ERROR`**: a server fault, message withheld.
- `/actions` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`) answers the same throw from an action body as **400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`**, with the driver spelling carried in `declaredCode`. That is a client refusal, and it puts the driver's own code on the wire.

Since #31271 (PR #31315), the MCP `run_action` and `resume_run` tools mirror `/actions`, so the divergence now governs two MCP tools as well as the REST door.

## Expected

A driver/database fault thrown inside an action body reads the same at `/actions` as at `/data`: a 5xx fault answer with no driver code on the wire. Unless the lane decides the 400 reading is right for action bodies, in which case `/data` and the tests should say why the two differ.

## Where to start

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts` and the `@objectstack/types` reader `actionsDoorAnswerOf` (added by #31271), compared with `dataDoorAnswerOf` (#31270).
- Pin: one row per door for a `SQLITE_BUSY`-coded throw, asserting the same status and code.

## Provenance

Out-of-scope finding 1 in the contract review on PR #31315 (#31271), which escalated it to the seat for a carrier.
